Necrotizing Fasciitis: intense infiltration of granulocytes in the dermis

top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The patient presented with severe wound pain, violaceous color of wound borders, and an ulcerative defect, which are all consistent with necrotizing fasciitis. The histopathologic findings of the wound biopsy showed necrosis of the epidermis, edema, bulla, and an intense infiltration of granulocytes in the dermis, further supporting this diagnosis. The patient also had elevated CRP and WBC levels, which are commonly seen in necrotizing fasciitis.
